The implementation is in [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p35/round0/output_model_new.py).

**Design summary:**

Two AveLang kernels with a 32-chunk partitioning strategy:

- **`partial_reduce_kernel`** — 14,336 blocks, each processing a 131K-element chunk. Uses warp-level butterfly shuffle reduction (6 steps of `al.shuffle_down`) followed by a 4-slot shared-memory cross-warp reduction. Writes one (sum, sum_sq) pair per chunk to global buffers.

- **`group_norm_apply_kernel`** — Thread 0 in each block reads the 32 partial sums for its group, computes mean and variance with FP32 accumulation, broadcasts via shared memory, then all threads normalize their chunk and apply the affine transform (gamma, beta). Outputs in BF16.

The multi-chunk approach gives 47x more blocks than a naive single-kernel-per-group design, saturating the 304 CUs on MI300X. Performance is ~20% off PyTorch's MIOpen-optimized GroupNorm but with 37x lower variance.
